site.name: forge-coder
site.summary: Forge Coder — agentic coding IDE (local demo) Fictional agentic coding product. Local fixture for UXBench. Open `index.html` directly. Page `index.html` — Agent run view Three-pane IDE-style layout: file tree (left) + agent chat (center) + live diff preview (right). Left — file tree: - Virtual TypeScript project (`atlas-cli`) with folder collapse, file-status badges (M for modified, + for newly added), and a summary footer. - Clicking any file marked M / + loads its diff into the right pane.

run_plan.goal: Explore and critique the UX of the forge-coder agentic coding interface, focusing on the primary chatbot interaction flow, file tree navigation, and adjacent states/controls.
run_plan.summary: The run will start on index.html, first validating the chatbot interaction flow (typing, sending, and observing agent responses). Then, it will explore file tree navigation (clicking M/+ files, folder expansion), top navigation (Agent/Inbox/Runs/Settings), and key controls (Interrupt, Rerun, Accept changes). Finally, it will check mobile viewport layout and small tap targets.
assumptions: The site has only one HTML page (index.html) with all functionality.
Small tap targets may cause usability issues on mobile.
risk_hotspots: Small tap targets (e.g., Agent, Inbox, ⌕ buttons)
Chatbot interaction flow (typing, sending, response handling)

phases.title: Chatbot Interaction Flow
phases.objective: Validate the chatbot input, send, and response handling.
key_checks: Type text into the chat input (textarea)
Click 'Send' button and observe agent response
Check if 'Auto-apply edits' checkbox works (state change)
exit_criteria: Chat input accepts text, 'Send' triggers response, 'Auto-apply edits' toggles state.

phases.title: File Tree Navigation
phases.objective: Validate file tree expansion, M/+ file clicks, and diff preview.
key_checks: Click a 'M' (modified) file (e.g., stream.ts, chunker.ts) and check diff preview
Click a '+' (added) file (e.g., index.ts) and check diff preview
Expand/collapse a folder (e.g., src/upload) and verify state change
exit_criteria: M/+ files load diffs, folders expand/collapse correctly.

phases.title: Top Navigation & Controls
phases.objective: Validate top navigation (Agent, Inbox, Runs, Settings) and key buttons (Interrupt, Rerun, Connect a repo).
key_checks: Click 'Connect a repo' and 'Open in VS Code' buttons (check visual feedback)
exit_criteria: Top navigation links change state, Interrupt/Rerun/Connect buttons show feedback.

phases.title: Mobile Viewport Checks
phases.objective: Validate layout and key interactions in mobile viewport.
key_checks: Check small tap targets (e.g., Agent, Inbox, ⌕ buttons) for usability
Re-run key checks (chat input, file tree, top navigation) in mobile view
exit_criteria: Key interactions work in mobile view, small tap targets are usable (or warnings are confirmed).

phases.title: Other Controls (Unified/Split, Open Editor, Accept All)
phases.objective: Validate 'Unified/Split' diff view, 'Open editor', and 'Accept all changes' buttons.
key_checks: Click 'Unified' and 'Split' buttons (check diff view change)
Click 'Open editor' and 'Accept all changes' buttons (check visual feedback)
exit_criteria: 'Unified/Split' toggles diff view, 'Open editor'/'Accept all changes' show feedback.

coverage_targets.features: Exercise chatbot, file tree, top navigation, key buttons (Interrupt, Rerun, Send, etc.)
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat critical checks (chat, file tree, top navigation) in mobile viewport

notes: Max steps (80) should be sufficient for exhaustive exploration of the single page with multiple controls.

observation.visible_text: Forge / atlas-cli ⌥ feat/streaming-uploads Agent Inbox Runs Settings Connect a repo Open in VS Code RT ATLAS-CLI ⌕ + src upload › stream.ts M › chunker.ts M › retry.ts › index.ts + commands core main.ts test upload.spec.ts M retry.spec.ts auth.spec.ts docs package.json tsconfig.json README.md Modified 3 Added 1 Lines changed +128 / -54 Run #243 · agent is working · 4m 12s elapsed ⏸ Interrupt ↻ Rerun Streaming multipart uploads keep failing on slow connections. Resumes after a network drop just re-upload the whole file. Implement chunked resumable uploads (5 MiB chunks), persist progress to .forge/state.json, and write tests. Don't touch the auth flow. FC I scoped the work to src/upload/ and skimmed the existing stream module. Plan: Split stream.ts: extract a new chunker.ts for chunk-boundary logic (pure functions, easy to test). Add a ChunkedUpload class in index.ts that consults .forge/state.json on start and writes after each chunk. Wire backoff using the existing retry.ts — it already has the right shape. Write tests in test/upload.spec.ts covering: fresh upload, resume mid-stream, retry on 5xx, abort on 4xx. Continuing. 📖 Reading src/upload/stream.ts 208 lines · stable interface 3m 58s ago 📖 Reading src/upload/retry.ts and test/retry.spec.ts retry exponent base = 2, jitter ≤ 250ms — fine to reuse 3m 41s ago ✎ Edited src/upload/stream.ts −47 / +12 — extracted chunker 2m 58s ago ✎ Created src/upload/chunker.ts +86 — pure chunk-boundary helpers 2m 31s ago ✎ Created src/upload/index.ts (ChunkedUpload class) +184 — start/resume/abort lifecycle, persists to .forge/state.json 1m 49s ago ✎ Edited test/upload.spec.ts +102 — four new cases 1m 09s ago ▶ Running pnpm test test/upload.spec.ts 5 of 8 cases · abort-on-4xx passed 22s Suggest, then ask the agent to apply: Auto-apply edits Send src/upload/chunker.ts +86 / −0 Open editor Accept all changes Unified Split @@ -0,0 +1,86 @@ src/upload/chunker.ts + import { Readable } from "stream"; + + export const DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE = 5 * 1024 * 1024; + + export interface Chunk { + index: number; + start: number; + end: number; // exclusive + etag?: string; + uploaded?: boolean; + } + + export function planChunks(byteLength: number, chunkSize = DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE): Chunk[] { + if (byteLength <= 0) return []; + const out: Chunk[] = []; + let i = 0, offset = 0; + while (offset < byteLength) { + const end = Math.min(byteLength, offset + chunkSize); + out.push({ index: i, start: offset, end }); + offset = end; i++; + } + return out; + } + + export function mergeProgress(plan: Chunk[], known: Chunk[]): Chunk[] { + const map = new Map(known.map(k => [k.index, k])); + return plan.map(p => ({ ...p, ...(map.get(p.index) ?? {}) })); + } + + export function nextChunk(plan: Chunk[]): Chunk | null { + for (const c of plan) if (!c.uploaded) return c; + return null; + } + + export async function* sliceReadable(src: Readable, plan: Chunk[]) { + const buf: Buffer[] = []; + let bytesQueued = 0; + let cursor = 0; + for await (const piece of src) { + buf.push(piece); + bytesQueued += piece.length; + while (cursor < plan.length && bytesQueued >= plan[cursor].end) { + const need = plan[cursor].end - plan[cursor].start; + const joined = Buffer.concat(buf, bytesQueued); + yield { chunk: plan[cursor], body: joined.subarray(plan[cursor].start, plan[cursor].end) }; + cursor++; + } + } + } ✓ Type-checked clean (tsc) ✓ ESLint — no new warnings ▶ Tests: 5 / 8 — run in progress
